>

There are reasons to ignore `<a name>`:
1. We want the model to be very simple because some decisions are made in the parser itself.
2. We've been advising developers to avoid`<a name>` for quite a while (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/a#name), so supporting it in a new feature doesn't seem right. There are no mentions of `<a name>` in any of the examples in the HTML standard.
3. This is consistent enough with other features that don't respect `name`, like `<label for>`.

> 
> This impacts `<link rel="expect" href="#ß" blocking="render">`. As written, the fragment (after parsing) is `#%C3%9F`. Which will not compare correctly to `<div id="ß">`. But we want those to match up. The trick is, we can't do a simple string comparison, because `<link rel="expect" href="#%C3%9F" blocking="render">` should ALSO match that `<div>`.

OK, I think the correct path is to share the parsing logic from "the indicated part of the document" but only match vs ID.
